program_name: Biotechnological and Chemical Sciences in Diagnostics (Italian administrative code 0102M22; the UNITO microsite also renders the name as 'Biotechnology and Chemical Sciences in Diagnostics')
teaching_language: Fully English-taught (100%). This is case (1): a stand-alone second-cycle degree whose official name and full curriculum are in English, not an English pathway inside an Italian-named degree, and not an interuniversity/joint degree. Apply@UniTo course record states 'Study language: English'; the programme's own Key Information page states 'Language: English'. It is a UNITO-only degree, but internally an INTERCLASS degree governed by two departments (Department of Molecular Biotechnologies and Health Sciences + Department of Chemistry) and organised by the School of Medicine. Teaching mode is declared as 'Blended (at least 10% ECTS offered online)'; the admission test itself is also run online via the UNITO Moodle platform. English proficiency at CEFR B2 is required because the course is delivered in English; no Italian-language requirement is stated for admission.
campus: Turin (Torino), Italy - 'Teaching site: Torino' / Apply@UniTo 'Study location: Italy, Turin'. University of Turin, Via Verdi 8, 10124 Torino. Departments involved: Molecular Biotechnologies and Health Sciences, and Chemistry; School of Medicine.
degree_class: Interclass LM-8 (Biotecnologie industriali / Industrial biotechnology) + LM-54 (Scienze chimiche / Chemical sciences), D.M. 270/04. Course code 0102M22. 120 ECTS, 2 years.
admission_type: Open access (non-restricted) with a mandatory verification of personal preparation. The UNITO microsite Key Information states 'Entry requirements: Course without restrictions in students' number'. Applications from abroad are filed through the Apply@UniTo (DreamApply) portal, which selects applicants against curricular requirements; candidates who do not qualify for exemption must pass a written online admission test. Note: although the programme has no numerus clausus, Apply@UniTo publishes a territory quota of 50 places for non-European applicants residing abroad. Because it is an OPEN-ACCESS postgraduate programme, it falls under the first admission call (all applicants) and the fourth admission call (EU/equivalent only) of the 2026/27 Apply@UniTo calendar - it is NOT in the third (restricted-number) call.
application_deadline_eu: 8 September 2026, 23:59:59 CET - fourth admission call for open-access postgraduate programmes, window 25 August - 8 September 2026, reserved to Italians, EU and EU-equivalent citizens and non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy (a.y. 2026/2027). EU/equivalent applicants may alternatively have used the first call (25 November 2025 - 29 January 2026), which was open to all applicants.
application_deadline_non_eu: 29 January 2026 - end of the FIRST admission call (25 November 2025 - 29 January 2026), the only 2026/27 window open to non-EU applicants residing abroad for postgraduate degree programmes. Non-EU applicants residing abroad cannot use the later calls (third, fourth and fifth calls are explicitly reserved to Italians, EU/EU-equivalents and non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy). This deadline has already passed as of the research date (1 September 2026); the equivalent 2027/28 first call had not yet been published. entry_exam_or_test: Written admission test (verification of adequate personal preparation), held online on the University of Turin Moodle platform. Structure: 50 multiple-choice questions - 30 Chemistry, 5 Physics/Mathematics, 15 Molecular/Cellular Biology; four options per question, one answer only, all questions equally weighted, 60 minutes total. A score of at least 60% is required to enrol. Topics follow a published Syllabus on the programme microsite; a mock test is offered. EXEMPTION: graduates of the Italian classes L-2 (Biotechnology), L-13 (Biological Sciences), L-27 (Chemical Technology Sciences) and L-29 (Pharmaceutical Technology Sciences) - or of other degree courses after positive evaluation by the Master Course Board - with a final degree grade of at least 99/110 are exempt from the test. Candidates are notified individually by e-mail (address given in the pre-registration form). No interview is required. The last test date published on the archived microsite was 13 September 2024, 11:00 - the 2026/27 test date could not be verified on a live page. [uncertain]
academic_requirements: 1) DEGREE LEVEL: a first-cycle degree (bachelor's) obtained after at least 3 years of university education - Italian laurea under D.M. 509 or D.M. 270, or an equivalent foreign qualification recognised as suitable under current legislation. Eligibility of foreign qualifications is approved by the Degree Course Council, and the degree/diploma certificate with the list of exams must be submitted and verified by the Evaluation Commission. 2) DIRECT-ACCESS CLASSES: Italian first-level degrees in classes L-2 Biotechnology, L-13 Biological Sciences, L-27 Chemical Technology Sciences, L-29 Pharmaceutical Technology Sciences (D.M. 270/04) or the equivalent D.M. 509/99 classes. 3) OTHER CLASSES / FOREIGN DEGREES - minimum curricular credits: at least 10 ECTS in at least one of MAT/01-MAT/09, FIS/01-FIS/08, INF/01; AND at least 18 ECTS in at least one of CHIM/01, CHIM/02, CHIM/03, CHIM/06, CHIM/08, CHIM/09, BIO/01, BIO/09, BIO/10, BIO/11, BIO/13, BIO/14, BIO/16, BIO/17, BIO/18, BIO/19. A tolerance of up to 15%, i.e. maximum 5 ECTS, is allowed, applicable to one or to several of the credit groups. 4) The Apply@UniTo course record expresses the same background requirement in exam terms: 'a solid background certified by at least 5 exams passed in the following subjects: Mathematics, Statistics, Physics, General and Inorganic Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, Biochemistry, Cell Biology, Molecular Biology and Genetics'. 5) PERSONAL PREPARATION: verified by the written online test unless exempt (degree grade >= 99/110 in L-2/L-13/L-27/L-29, or another degree class positively evaluated by the Master Course Board). 6) PLACES: the programme is open access (no numerus clausus); Apply@UniTo publishes a territory quota of 50 available places for non-European applicants residing abroad. 7) Programme size: 120 ECTS over 2 years; students choose full-time or part-time status for each year of enrolment, with tuition varying accordingly.
language_requirements: English at CEFR B2 or higher. For applications submitted through Apply@UniTo the requirement is an INTERNATIONAL CERTIFICATE, no more than three years old, from the accepted list: Cambridge CPE; Cambridge CAE; Cambridge FCE with minimum score 173 (grade B); PTE Academic minimum 65; IELTS minimum 5.5 out of 9 with no component below 5.5; TOEFL iBT minimum 69 out of 120 with no component below 17; Trinity College ISE II. The programme microsite's own Admission Requirements page (last updated 30/06/2025) states the softer wording: 'Since the course will be delivered in English, it will be necessary to document an English proficiency corresponding to the B2 level ... or higher (self-declaration is allowed)' - self-declaration should be treated as applying to domestic enrolment procedures only; international applicants filing on Apply@UniTo should provide one of the listed certificates. [uncertain] No Italian-language requirement is set for admission (free Italian courses are offered to enrolled international students via https://en.unito.it/services/learning-italian).
required_documents: Via the Apply@UniTo portal: 1) first-cycle (bachelor's) degree certificate/diploma with transcript of records listing the exams passed and credits, used to verify the curricular requirements; 2) English language certificate at CEFR B2 or above from the accepted list, issued no more than 3 years before; 3) MOTIVATION LETTER - explicitly listed under 'Other requirements' on the Apply@UniTo course page ('A motivation letter must be added to your application'), in English or Italian; 4) identity document / passport and the documents required for the applicant's specific foreign education system (see Apply@UniTo 'Required documentation'); 5) optional but recommended: degree programme syllabus / course descriptions issued by the foreign institution, with translation into Italian, English, French or Spanish; 6) proof of payment of the EUR 60 non-refundable application fee, paid within the deadline of the call (same amount whether one or two programmes are selected). LANGUAGES: entry-qualification documents are accepted in English, French, Italian or Spanish; a document in any other language must be uploaded together with a certified translation. AFTER SUBMISSION: UNITO may request further documents such as the Declaration of Value (Dichiarazione di Valore), Statement of Verification or CIMEA Statement of Comparability, and the International Students Office may request additional documentation at the enrolment stage.

uncertainty_notes: 1) SOURCE ACCESS: en.unito.it and www.unito.it return 403 to automated fetches, and bcsd.campusnet.unito.it is refused/timed out at network level; the programme microsite content above was therefore read from Internet Archive snapshots (home 2026-05-05, admission_requirements 2025-10-12, Test 2025-03-16, key_information 2025-01-18). Only the Apply@UniTo pages (course 698, call calendar, required documentation) were read live on 2026-09-01. Microsite content may have been updated since those snapshots. 2) TWO DIFFERENT WORDINGS OF THE CURRICULAR REQUIREMENT: Apply@UniTo asks for 'at least 5 exams passed' in a list of subjects, while the microsite states ECTS thresholds (10 ECTS maths/physics/informatics + 18 ECTS chemistry/biology SSD groups, 15%/5 ECTS tolerance). These are two formulations of the same rule for different audiences; an applicant should satisfy both readings. 3) LANGUAGE EVIDENCE CONFLICT: the microsite allows self-declaration of B2 English, whereas Apply@UniTo requires one of the listed international certificates issued within the last 3 years. For international applicants the Apply@UniTo rule is the operative one; the self-declaration wording is marked uncertain. 4) ADMISSION TEST DATE for a.y. 2026/27 is NOT verified - the only date found (13 September 2024, 11:00) comes from an archived page last updated in June 2024. The test format (50 questions, 60 minutes, >=60% pass) is from the same archived page and may have changed. 5) DEADLINES: the 8 September 2026 date is read live from the Apply@UniTo course page and matches the fourth-call window in the official calendar; the non-EU (residing abroad) date of 29 January 2026 is derived from the official calendar's first call, which is the only 2026/27 window open to non-EU applicants abroad for postgraduate programmes - the course page itself, viewed from a non-EU location, displayed only the currently open EU-restricted call, so the non-EU date is inferred from the calendar rather than shown on the course record. Both 2026/27 windows are already closed as of 1 September 2026 except the EU call closing 8 September 2026. 6) The '50 available places for non-European applicants residing abroad' is a territory quota on an otherwise open-access programme, not a numerus clausus - do not present the degree as restricted access. 7) The degree is an INTERCLASS degree (LM-8 / LM-54) run jointly by two UNITO departments; it is NOT an interuniversity or joint/double degree with another university. 8) Teaching mode is officially 'Blended (at least 10% ECTS offered online)' per the microsite Key Information page (snapshot of a 2024 update); whether this still holds for 2026/27 is unverified. 9) The 'Talents 4 UniTo' scholarship availability for this specific programme comes from search-result summaries of en.unito.it / apply.unito.it pages that could not be opened directly; treat as indicative.
